checks.details: In this pinned export only one reason pair ever reaches the function: route.zai-coding-plan.glm-5-3-flash, input 'Coding Plan subscription; models.dev lists 0 for every per-token cost on this plan, which is a zero marginal price inside the plan, not a measured bill' and output 'Coding Plan subscription; models.dev lists 0' — the output is a literal prefix of the input, so the dropped copy loses nothing and both proofs assert exactly that. Class OBSERVATION (latent, unreachable by this export), with two concrete inputs: (1) semantic loss — kept 'this route is not the Coding Plan subscription', new 'Coding Plan subscription' is dropped because substring containment is not logical subsumption, so the export's independent positive statement survives only inside a negation and the join asserts only the keeper; (2) order asymmetry — the skip test checks only kept.contains(new), so reasons [Some('Coding Plan subscription'), Some('Coding Plan subscription; not a measured bill')] keep both and the join repeats the clause, the very defect S-16 removed; it recurs whenever the fuller reason is the output side. The doc comment states the route-specific reasoning (input is the fuller of the two), so the function is correct for this export and every proof holds; the general contract is order-dependent and untested beyond the glm pair
